question: How do they match annotators to instances?

answer.free_form_answer: Annotations from experts are used if they have already been collected.
evidence: So far a system was trained on one type of data, either labeled by crowd or experts. We now examine the performance of a system trained on data that was routed to either experts or crowd annotators depending on their predicted difficult. Given the results presented so far mixing annotators may be beneficial given their respective trade-offs of precision and recall. We use the annotations from experts for an abstract if it exists otherwise use crowd annotations. The results are presented in Table 6 .

title: Predicting Annotation Difficulty to Improve Task Routing and Model Performance for Biomedical Information Extraction
answer_short: They match instances to annotators based on predicted difficulty scores, routing difficult ones to domain experts and easier ones to crowd annotators.
answer_rationale: The evidence indicates that instances are matched to annotators using predicted difficulty scores. Text 5 explicitly states that 'assigning instances predicted to be difficult to domain experts is an effective strategy for task routing.' Text 4 supports this by noting that 'simulations in which difficult examples are routed to experts and other instances to crowd annotators yields the best results.' Text 3 also aligns with this by discussing routing difficult instances to domain experts and easier ones to crowd annotators as a simulated strategy. Together, these sources confirm the mechanism of matching based on difficulty scores.
